q: How many major planets orbit the Sun in our Solar System?
What is Earth's only natural satellite?
List the 8 planets of our Solar System in increasing order of distance from the Sun.
a: 1. Mercury, 2. Venus, 3. Earth, 4. Mars, 5. Jupiter, 6. Saturn, 7. Uranus, 8. Neptune.

q: What is a Constellation? Give two prominent examples.
a: A constellation is a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern in the night sky named after figures or objects. Examples: Saptarishi (Ursa Major / Big Dipper) and Orion (The Hunter).

q: How can you locate the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara) in the northern night sky using Saptarishi?
a: Locate the two outer pointer stars on the bowl of the Saptarishi constellation and extend an imaginary straight line upward; the line points directly to the fixed Pole Star marking true North.

q: Why is Pluto classified as a Dwarf Planet rather than an official planet?
a: In 2006, the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto because it has not cleared its orbital neighborhood of other celestial debris.

q: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is closer to the Sun?
a: Venus has a thick atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide, which traps solar heat through an extreme runaway greenhouse effect.
